items.t: 40 mg dose: only for severe hypercholesterolaemia at high cardiovascular risk not at goal on 20 mg, with routine follow-up; specialist supervision recommended when starting 40 mg.

items.t: Start 5 mg or 10 mg once daily (statin-naive or switching). May go up one dose level after 4 weeks. Maximum 40 mg only in selected patients (see restrictions).

src.q: The recommended start dose is 5 or 10 mg orally once daily in both statin naïve or patients switched from another HMG CoA reductase inhibitor.

items.t: 20 mg daily was the dose used in the risk-reduction study.

items.t: Start 5 mg in: patients over 70 years; moderate renal impairment (CrCl <60 mL/min); Asian ancestry; patients with factors predisposing to myopathy. 40 mg is contraindicated in Asian patients and in moderate renal impairment.

items.t: Known SLCO1B1 c.521CC or ABCG2 c.421AA genotype: half the usual dose, maximum 20 mg once daily.

items.t: With medicines that raise rosuvastatin exposure about 2-fold or more: start 5 mg once daily and limit the maximum dose so exposure does not exceed that of 40 mg alone (e.g. 20 mg with gemfibrozil).

src.q: Start with a 5 mg once daily dose of Crestor if the expected increase in exposure (AUC) is approximately 2-fold or higher.

items.t: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, 6-17 years: usual start 5 mg daily. Age 6-9: 5-10 mg once daily (doses above 10 mg not studied). Age 10-17: 5-20 mg once daily (doses above 20 mg not studied).

src.q: In children and adolescents with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia the usual start dose is 5 mg daily.
In children 6 to 9 years of age with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, the usual dose range is 5-10 mg orally once daily.
In children 10 to 17 years of age with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, the usual dose range is 5-20 mg orally once daily.

items.t: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, 6-17 years: start 5-10 mg once daily; maximum 20 mg once daily.

src.q: In children 6 to 17 years of age with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, the recommended maximum dose is 20 mg once daily.
A starting dose of 5 to 10 mg once daily depending on age, weight and prior statin use is advised.

items.t: Muscle: myalgia, myopathy and rarely rhabdomyolysis, especially above 20 mg. Prescribe with caution if predisposed (renal impairment, hypothyroidism, hereditary muscle disorder, previous statin/fibrate muscle toxicity, alcohol abuse, age >70, raised plasma levels, fibrates). items.t: Do not use in an acute serious condition suggesting myopathy or predisposing to renal failure from rhabdomyolysis (e.g. sepsis, hypotension, major surgery, trauma, severe metabolic, endocrine or electrolyte disorders, uncontrolled seizures).

items.t: Liver: caution with excessive alcohol intake or a history of liver disease. Stop or reduce the dose if transaminases exceed 3 x ULN.

src.q: Crestor should be used with caution in patients who consume excessive quantities of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease.
Crestor should be discontinued or the dose reduced if the level of serum transaminases is greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal.

items.t: Severe cutaneous reactions (SJS, DRESS) reported: stop immediately if signs appear and never restart after SJS or DRESS.

src.q: Crestor should be discontinued immediately and an alternative treatment should be considered

items.t: Myasthenia gravis may start or worsen with statins; stop if symptoms worsen.

src.q: Crestor should be discontinued in case of aggravation of symptoms.

items.t: Diabetes risk: statins may raise blood glucose; monitor patients at risk (fasting glucose 5.6-6.9 mmol/L, BMI >30 kg/m2, raised triglycerides, hypertension). This is not a reason to stop treatment.

src.q: Patients at risk (fasting glucose 5.6 to 6.9 mmol/l, BMI >30 kg/m2, raised triglycerides, hypertension) should be monitored both clinically and biochemically according to national guidelines.

items.t: Systemic fusidic acid: do not co-administer, or within 7 days of stopping it (rhabdomyolysis, some fatal).

src.q: Crestor must not be co-administered with systemic formulations of fusidic acid or within 7 days of stopping fusidic acid treatment.

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Fibrates (including fenofibrate): increased risk of myopathy. 40 mg contraindicated with a fibrate; start with 5 mg. Gemfibrozil is not recommended. MHRA: with fibrates start 5 mg and do not exceed 20 mg.

src.q: The 40 mg dose is contraindicated with concomitant use of a fibrate (see sections 4.3 and 4.4). These patients should also start with the 5 mg dose.

items.t: Warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists: starting or increasing rosuvastatin may raise INR; stopping or reducing it may lower INR. Monitor INR.

src.q: may result in an increase in International Normalised Ratio (INR)

items.t: Ezetimibe: small rise in rosuvastatin exposure; a pharmacodynamic interaction (muscle adverse effects) cannot be ruled out. Use with caution.

items.t: Aluminium/magnesium hydroxide antacid: taken at the same time, rosuvastatin levels fall by about 50%; giving the antacid 2 hours after rosuvastatin lessens this.

This effect was mitigated when the antacid was dosed 2 hours after Crestor.

items.t: Febuxostat: raises rosuvastatin exposure about 1.9-fold. Ciclosporin (7-fold; contraindicated), ticagrelor, certain HIV/hepatitis C protease inhibitors and others in SmPC Table 1 also raise levels: consider alternatives or dose adjustment.
